name: Fokker-Planck (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Process)

analytic_solution.description: Gaussian(mu(t), sigma_sq(t)) where mu(t)=mu_0*exp(-t), sigma_sq(t) = D/gamma + (sigma_0_sq - D/gamma)*exp(-2*gamma*t) with D=1, gamma=1

notes: The drift term (x*p)_x drives the mean toward zero while diffusion broadens the distribution. At steady state, the solution is N(0,1). Variable-coefficient advection requires careful discretization.

name: Focusing Nonlinear Schrodinger Equation (1-Soliton)

boundary_conditions.note: Domain is large enough that sech(x) is effectively zero at boundaries (~1e-13), so periodic BCs are appropriate for spectral methods

notes: Complex-valued dispersive PDE requiring split-step or similar method. The L2 norm integral(|psi|^2 dx) is a conserved quantity (mass). Strang splitting gives O(dt^2) global error.

name: 2D Helmholtz Equation (Manufactured Solution)

source_term.note: Derived from manufactured solution via substitution into the PDE

notes: The operator -laplacian - k^2 I is indefinite since k^2=100 exceeds the first eigenvalue of -laplacian (2*pi^2 ~ 19.74). Requires a direct solver or appropriate iterative method for indefinite systems. With the 5-point FD stencil, the nearest discrete eigenvalue to k^2=100 is approximately pi^2*10 ~ 98.7, but the manufactured solution only excites the (1,1) mode (eigenvalue 2*pi^2), so the system is well-conditioned for this specific RHS.
